[Sun 2026-10-11 16:12 GMT+8] Read the context documents in context.txt and answer the following question.

Context: twenty two.Reasonable people will not resist the law violently, unless the consequences of resisting the law are no worse than obeying the law, thus desperate....

Question: Which of the following expressions does not agree with the expression above?

Options:
A. A.Only if the consequences of violent resistance to the law are no worse than obedience to the law, rational people will desperately and violently resist the law.
B. B.If the consequences of violent resistance to the law are worse than obedience to the law, rational people will not desperately violently resist the law.
C. C.If the consequences of obeying the law are better than violent resistance, the rational person will not desperately violently resist the law.
D. D.Only the consequences of violent resistance to the law are worse than obedience to the law.Reasonable people will not desperately violently resist the law.

IMPORTANT: You must ONLY output the option letter (A, B, C, or D) to 'answer.txt' in the workspace.

**CRITICAL**: Do NOT write the full text of the answer. Only write a single letter: A, B, C, or D.


**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 360s.

content.thinking:
Let me analyze the logic. The statement: "Reasonable people will not resist the law violently, unless the consequences of resisting the law are no worse than obeying the law, thus desperate."

Formal: Not-violently-resist unless (consequences of resistance ≤ consequences of obeying). "Unless P, Q" = if not P then Q... Actually "Q unless P" = "if not P then Q", equivalent "Q or P". So: "will not violently resist unless (consequences of resistance are no worse than obeying)" = if NOT(consequences of resistance no worse than obeying) then will not violently resist. I.e., if consequences of resistance are worse than obeying, then reasonable people will not violently resist. Equivalently, only if consequences of resistance are no worse than obeying will they violently resist.

Option A: "Only if the consequences of violent resistance are no worse than obedience, rational people will desperately violently resist." That matches: violent resistance only if consequences no worse. Agrees.

Option B: "If the consequences of violent resistance are worse than obedience, rational people will not desperately violently resist." This is the contrapositive — agrees.

Option C: "If the consequences of obeying the law are better than violent resistance, the rational person will not desperately violently resist the law." Consequences of obeying better than resistance = resistance worse than obeying → will not resist. That agrees too.

Wait, "consequences of obeying are better than violent resistance" means obeying is better, i.e., resistance worse → not resist. Agrees.

Option D: "Only the consequences of violent resistance to the law are worse than obedience to the law. Reasonable people will not desperately violently resist the law." Hmm, this says "Only if consequences of violent resistance are WORSE than obedience, reasonable people will not violently resist." That's: not resist only if resistance worse. But original: not resist unless resistance no worse... actually original: they will not violently resist unless consequences of resistance no worse than obeying. Means they may violently resist only when resistance is no worse. So "not resist" happens when resistance is worse. D says: only if resistance is worse, will not resist — i.e., if resistance is no worse, they WILL resist. That's stronger than original (original doesn't guarantee they resist when no worse; only permits). But strictly, "not resist unless P" means not-resist occurs only when... hmm.

Actually "Q unless P" literally: Q holds except when P. So "not resist unless (resistance no worse)" = not-resist holds except when resistance is no worse; when resistance is no worse, not-resist may or may not hold. So "not-resist" → P? If not-resist holds except when P... The standard logical translation: "Q unless P" ≡ "Q or P" ≡ "if not P then Q". So: if resistance is worse than obeying → not resist. Contrapositive: if resist → resistance no worse.

D: "Only if resistance worse → not resist" i.e., not-resist only if resistance worse = if not-resist then resistance worse. That's not equivalent; it's affirming the consequent direction. Actually original: resistance worse → not resist. D: not resist → resistance worse. Not equivalent. So D disagrees.

Answer: D.
